subproblems.title: Hilbert–Schmidt identity Σ_j α(f∘j)² = n!·|α|² for an orthonormal basis f (reused accepted DAG theorem)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let α be an n-covector on ℝ^P (a continuous alternating n-linear form, Covector (Euclid P) n) and let f = (f_0, …, f_{P−1}) be an orthonormal basis of ℝ^P indexed by Fin P. Then Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} α(f_{j(0)}, …, f_{j(n−1)})² = n!·|α|_E², where |α|_E = covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2} and e is the standard basis. (This is exactly the comparator-accepted DAG theorem regcomp_covector_sq_sum_orthonormalBasis, reused here with its identical frozen Lean type; it is Fact (O) of the parent proof.)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n) (f : OrthonormalBasis (Fin P) ℝ (Euclid P)), ∑ j : Fin n → Fin P, (α (fun k => f (j k))) ^ 2 = (n.factorial : ℝ) * covectorEuclideanNorm α ^ 2
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Fact (O) of the parent proof (orthogonal invariance of the coefficient norm), in the form already accepted for the DAG node root.regular_components_are_minimizing-a1.imrep_mass_formula-a1.covector_sq_sum-a1 (declaration regcomp_covector_sq_sum_orthonormalBasis, identical frozen type). Notation: e_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i; for a family b : Fin P → ℝ^P and j : Fin n → Fin P write b∘j := (b_{j(0)}, …, b_{j(n−1)}); S_b(α) := Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} α(b∘j)². We must show S_f(α) = n!·|α|_E².
1. (Square of the norm.) The radicand Σ_I [I strictly increasing] α(e∘I)² is a finite sum of nonnegative terms, so |α|_E² = Σ_{I strictly increasing} α(e∘I)² (Real.sq_sqrt).
2. (Basis independence by slotwise Parseval.) Let b, b' be orthonormal bases of ℝ^P indexed by Fin P. For m = 0, 1, …, n put H_m := Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} α(w_m(j))², where w_m(j)(k) := b_{j(k)} if k < m and w_m(j)(k) := b'_{j(k)} if k ≥ m. Then H_0 = S_{b'}(α) and H_n = S_b(α). Fix m < n and split every j into its m-th value i := j(m) and its values j' on the other n − 1 slots (j ↦ (j(m), j') is a bijection, e.g. via Fin.insertNth / Fin.removeNth). For fixed j' the map λ_{j'}(x) := α(u_0, …, u_{m−1}, x, u_{m+1}, …, u_{n−1}) with u_k := b_{j(k)} for k < m and u_k := b'_{j(k)} for k > m is a linear functional of x ∈ ℝ^P; writing λ_{j'}(x) = ⟨r, x⟩ with r := Σ_a λ_{j'}(e_a)e_a, Parseval for orthonormal bases (OrthonormalBasis.sum_sq_inner_right) gives Σ_i λ_{j'}(b_i)² = ‖r‖² = Σ_i λ_{j'}(b'_i)². The terms of H_{m+1} with fixed j' are the λ_{j'}(b_i)² and those of H_m are the λ_{j'}(b'_i)²; summing over j' gives H_{m+1} = H_m. By induction on m, S_b(α) = S_{b'}(α); in particular S_f(α) = S_e(α).
3. (Non-injective tuples.) If j is not injective then e∘j is not injective, so α(e∘j) = 0 (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_eq_zero_of_not_injective). Hence S_e(α) = Σ_{j injective} α(e∘j)².
4. (Injective tuples = increasing tuples × permutations.) Every injective j : Fin n → Fin P factors uniquely as j = I∘π with I strictly increasing and π ∈ Perm(Fin n): with σ := Tuple.sort j, j∘σ is monotone (Tuple.monotone_sort) and injective, hence strictly increasing; take I := j∘σ, π := σ⁻¹. Uniqueness: I∘π = I'∘π' forces range I = range I', and a strictly increasing map Fin n → Fin P is determined by its range (StrictMono.range_inj / Finset.orderEmbOfFin_unique), so I = I' and then π = π' (I injective). Conversely each I∘π is injective.
5. (Signs.) α(e∘I∘π) = sign(π)·α(e∘I) (AlternatingMap.map_perm), so α(e∘(I∘π))² = α(e∘I)².
6. (Counting.) By steps 3–5, S_e(α) = Σ_{I strictly increasing} Σ_{π ∈ Perm(Fin n)} α(e∘I)² = n!·Σ_{I strictly increasing} α(e∘I)² = n!·|α|_E² (Fintype.card_perm, Fintype.card_fin, step 1).
7. (Conclusion.) Σ_j α(f∘j)² = S_f(α) = S_e(α) = n!·|α|_E² by steps 2 and 6. The argument covers n = 0 (one empty tuple, strictly increasing; 0! = 1) and n > P (no injective and no strictly increasing tuples; both sides 0). ∎
proof_key_steps: |α|_E² is the sum of α(e∘I)² over strictly increasing I.
Slotwise Parseval (hybrid sums H_m) shows Σ_j α(b∘j)² is independent of the orthonormal basis b.
Non-injective tuples contribute 0; injective tuples are exactly I∘π and contribute α(e∘I)² each.
Counting the n! permutations gives Σ_j α(e∘j)² = n!·|α|_E², hence Σ_j α(f∘j)² = n!·|α|_E².

subproblems.title: Coefficient-norm bounds for evaluation on, and pull-back by, an orthonormal frame
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let v = (v_0, …, v_{n−1}) be an orthonormal family in ℝ^P = Euclid P and let pL : ℝ^P → ℝⁿ be a continuous linear map with (pL x)_i = ⟨v_i, x⟩ for all x ∈ ℝ^P and i ∈ Fin n. Then (a) |β(v_0, …, v_{n−1})| ≤ |β| for every n-covector β on ℝ^P, and (b) for every l ∈ ℕ and every l-covector γ on ℝⁿ, the pulled-back covector γ∘pL (i.e. γ.compContinuousLinearMap pL, (γ∘pL)(u_1, …, u_l) = γ(pL u_1, …, pL u_l)) satisfies |γ∘pL| ≤ |γ|. Here |·| = covectorEuclideanNorm on Covector (Euclid P) _ resp. Covector (Euclid n) _.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (v : Fin n → Euclid P) (pL : Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid n), Orthonormal ℝ v → (∀ (x : Euclid P) (i : Fin n), pL x i = inner ℝ (v i) x) → (∀ β : Covector (Euclid P) n, |β v| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm β) ∧ ∀ (l : ℕ) (γ : Covector (Euclid n) l), covectorEuclideanNorm (γ.compContinuousLinearMap pL) ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm γ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Fact (O), consequences (O1) and (O3), of the parent proof. Uses the sibling sq_sum (regcomp_covector_sq_sum_orthonormalBasis): for every m, every orthonormal basis b : OrthonormalBasis (Fin m) ℝ (Euclid m) and every l-covector α on ℝ^m, Σ_{j : Fin l → Fin m} α(b∘j)² = l!·|α|²  (★).
1. (n ≤ P.) v is orthonormal, hence linearly independent (Orthonormal.linearIndependent), so n = card(Fin n) ≤ finrank ℝ (Euclid P) = P (LinearIndependent.fintype_card_le_finrank, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin). Let ι := Fin.castLE (n ≤ P) : Fin n → Fin P (injective).
2. (Extension of v to an orthonormal basis.) Define v' : Fin P → ℝ^P by v'(ι i) := v_i and v'(m) := 0 for m ∉ range ι, and s := range ι. The restriction s.domRestrict v' is v reindexed by the bijection Fin n ≃ s induced by ι, hence orthonormal. By Orthonormal.exists_orthonormalBasis_extension_of_card_eq (finrank (Euclid P) = P = card (Fin P)) there is f : OrthonormalBasis (Fin P) ℝ (Euclid P) with f(ι i) = v_i for all i ∈ Fin n.
3. (pL on the basis.) For i ∈ Fin n: (pL f(ι i))_k = ⟨v_k, v_i⟩ = δ_{ki}, so pL(f(ι i)) = e_i (ext on Euclid n). For m ∉ range ι, f_m is orthogonal to every f(ι k) = v_k (distinct members of an orthonormal basis), so (pL f_m)_k = ⟨v_k, f_m⟩ = 0 for all k, i.e. pL f_m = 0.
4. (Proof of (b).) Let α := γ∘pL ∈ Λ^l(ℝ^P). By (★) on ℝ^P with b := f: l!·|α|² = Σ_{j : Fin l → Fin P} γ(pL f_{j(1)}, …, pL f_{j(l)})². If some value j(k) ∉ range ι, the k-th argument pL f_{j(k)} is 0 and the term vanishes (multilinearity, ContinuousMultilinearMap.map_coord_zero). The remaining j are exactly ι∘j' with j' : Fin l → Fin n (bijectively, ι injective), and for them the term is γ(e∘j')² by step 3. Hence l!·|α|² = Σ_{j' : Fin l → Fin n} γ(e∘j')² = l!·|γ|² by (★) on ℝⁿ with the standard orthonormal basis EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ. Since l! > 0 and both norms are ≥ 0 (covectorEuclideanNorm_nonneg), |γ∘pL| = |γ|, in particular |γ∘pL| ≤ |γ|. (Formally: the sum over Fin l → Fin P splits as the sum over the image of j' ↦ ι∘j' (Finset.sum_image, injective) plus terms that are 0 (Finset.sum_subset).)
5. (Proof of (a).) By (★) on ℝ^P with b := f and l := n: n!·|β|² = Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} β(f∘j)². All terms are ≥ 0, and π ↦ ι∘π is an injective map Perm(Fin n) → (Fin n → Fin P), so the sum is ≥ Σ_{π ∈ Perm(Fin n)} β(f∘ι∘π)² (Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg after Finset.sum_image). For every π, f∘ι∘π = v∘π (step 2) and β(v∘π) = sign(π)·β(v) (AlternatingMap.map_perm applied to β.toAlternatingMap), so each of these n! terms equals β(v)². Hence n!·|β|² ≥ n!·β(v)², so β(v)² ≤ |β|² and, as |β| ≥ 0, |β(v)| ≤ |β| (abs_le_of_sq_le / sq_le_sq'). ∎
proof_key_steps: Orthonormality gives n ≤ P; extend v to an orthonormal basis f of ℝ^P with f∘castLE = v.
pL maps f(castLE i) to e_i and every other basis vector to 0.
Apply the identity Σ_j α(f∘j)² = l!|α|² to α = γ∘pL on ℝ^P and to γ on ℝⁿ: the sums coincide, so |γ∘pL| = |γ|.
For β on ℝ^P the n! permutation tuples v∘π each contribute β(v)², so n!|β|² ≥ n!β(v)² and |β(v)| ≤ |β|.

subproblems.title: The coordinate projection pushes Hⁿ on an affine n-plane forward to Lebesgue measure
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let v = (v_0, …, v_{n−1}) be orthonormal in ℝ^P, w ∈ ℝ^P, Π := {y ∈ ℝ^P : y − w ∈ span(v)}, and let pL : ℝ^P → ℝⁿ be a continuous linear map with (pL x)_i = ⟨v_i, x⟩ for all x, i. Then the push-forward of Hⁿ⌞Π (Hⁿ = μHE[n] on ℝ^P) under pL is Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ: Measure.map pL (μHE[n].restrict Π) = volume on Euclid n.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (v : Fin n → Euclid P) (w : Euclid P) (pL : Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid n), Orthonormal ℝ v → (∀ (x : Euclid P) (i : Fin n), pL x i = inner ℝ (v i) x) → Measure.map pL ((μHE[n]).restrict {y : Euclid P | y - w ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range v)}) = (volume : Measure (Euclid n))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 0, 8 and 12 of the parent proof ('p|_{V₀+w} is an isometry onto ℝⁿ and Hⁿ = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume, Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure').
1. (A parametrisation of Π.) Define ι : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P, ι(z) := w + Σ_i (z_i − ⟨v_i, w⟩)·v_i. It is continuous (affine), hence measurable.
2. (pL∘ι = id.) (pL ι(z))_k = ⟨v_k, w⟩ + Σ_i (z_i − ⟨v_i, w⟩)⟨v_k, v_i⟩ = ⟨v_k, w⟩ + z_k − ⟨v_k, w⟩ = z_k by orthonormality; so pL(ι z) = z (ext on Euclid n).
3. (ι is an isometry.) ι(z) − ι(z') = Σ_i (z_i − z'_i)v_i and, v being orthonormal, ‖Σ_i c_i v_i‖² = Σ_i c_i² (Orthonormal.inner_sum / norm_sq of an orthonormal combination), which is ‖z − z'‖² in Euclid n (EuclideanSpace.norm_eq). So dist(ι z, ι z') = dist(z, z') (Isometry.of_dist_eq).
4. (range ι = Π.) If y = ι(z) then y − w = Σ_i c_i v_i ∈ span(v). Conversely, if y − w ∈ span(v), write y − w = Σ_i c_i v_i (Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun); taking inner products with v_k gives c_k = ⟨v_k, y − w⟩. With z := pL y (z_i = ⟨v_i, y⟩) we get ι(z) = w + Σ_i (⟨v_i, y⟩ − ⟨v_i, w⟩)v_i = w + Σ_i ⟨v_i, y − w⟩v_i = w + (y − w) = y.
5. (Hausdorff measure.) By Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure, Measure.map ι μHE[n] = μHE[n].restrict (range ι) = μHE[n].restrict Π (μHE[n] on Euclid n on the left, on Euclid P on the right), and μHE[n] = volume on Euclid n (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume n).

subproblems.title: A 1-Lipschitz function isolating one of finitely many parallel planes
subproblems.statement: Let P, n, N ∈ ℕ, let v = (v_0, …, v_{n−1}) be orthonormal in ℝ^P, V₀ := span(v), w_0, …, w_{N−1} ∈ ℝ^P pairwise distinct with ⟨w_i, v_j⟩ = 0 for all i, j, α_0, …, α_{N−1} ∈ ℝ, Π_i := {y : y − w_i ∈ V₀}, ν := Σ_i ofReal(α_i)·Hⁿ⌞Π_i (Hⁿ = μHE[n]), pL : ℝ^P → ℝⁿ continuous linear with (pL x)_i = ⟨v_i, x⟩, and i₀ ∈ Fin N. Then there are g : ℝ^P → ℝ and δ > 0 such that g is 1-Lipschitz, g = 0 on Π_{i₀}, ν⌞{g < 3δ} = ofReal(α_{i₀})·Hⁿ⌞Π_{i₀}, and for all real t, r the set {g ≤ t} ∩ pL⁻¹(closedBall(0, r)) is compact.

Source: steps 0 and 1 of the parent proof (g := dist(·, V₀ + w), δ' := min_{j≠i₀}|w_j − w|/3, compactness of p⁻¹(B̄_{3R}) ∩ {δ' ≤ g ≤ 2δ'}).
1. (Orthogonal decomposition.) For x ∈ ℝ^P put Q(x) := x − Σ_j ⟨v_j, x⟩v_j. Q is linear, ⟨v_k, Q x⟩ = ⟨v_k, x⟩ − Σ_j ⟨v_j, x⟩⟨v_k, v_j⟩ = 0, and x = Σ_j ⟨v_j, x⟩v_j + Q x with orthogonal summands, so ‖x‖² = ‖Σ_j ⟨v_j, x⟩v_j‖² + ‖Q x‖² = ‖pL x‖² + ‖Q x‖² (Pythagoras, norm_add_sq_eq_norm_sq_add_norm_sq_of_inner_eq_zero; ‖Σ_j c_j v_j‖² = Σ_j c_j² = ‖pL x‖² for c_j = ⟨v_j, x⟩ = (pL x)_j). In particular ‖Q x‖ ≤ ‖x‖. If y ∈ V₀, y = Σ_j c_j v_j, then ⟨v_j, y⟩ = c_j and Q y = 0; if y ⊥ v_j for all j then Q y = y.
2. (Definition of g.) Let w := w_{i₀} and g(x) := ‖Q(x − w)‖ ≥ 0. Since Q is linear, |g x − g x'| ≤ ‖Q(x − x')‖ ≤ ‖x − x'‖ (abs_norm_sub_norm_le), so g is 1-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul), in particular continuous.
3. (Values on the planes.) Let y ∈ Π_j. Then Q(y − w) = Q(y − w_j) + Q(w_j − w) = 0 + (w_j − w), because y − w_j ∈ V₀ and w_j − w ⊥ v_k for all k (⟨w_j, v_k⟩ = ⟨w, v_k⟩ = 0). Hence g ≡ ‖w_j − w‖ on Π_j: g = 0 on Π_{i₀}, and g > 0 on Π_j for j ≠ i₀ (w injective).
4. (Choice of δ.) The finitely many numbers ‖w_j − w‖, j ≠ i₀, are positive. Let δ := (1/3)·min_{j ∈ Fin N} c_j with c_j := 1 if j = i₀ and c_j := ‖w_j − w‖ otherwise (Finset.univ.inf' over the nonempty Fin N, which contains i₀). Then δ > 0 and 3δ ≤ ‖w_j − w‖ for j ≠ i₀, so Π_j ∩ {g < 3δ} = ∅ for j ≠ i₀, while Π_{i₀} ⊆ {g = 0} ⊆ {g < 3δ}.
5. (The restriction.) {g < 3δ} is open, hence measurable. For a measurable set B: ν⌞{g<3δ}(B) = ν(B ∩ {g<3δ}) = Σ_i ofReal(α_i)·Hⁿ(B ∩ {g<3δ} ∩ Π_i) (Measure.restrict_apply, Measure.coe_finset_sum / Finset.sum_apply, Measure.smul_apply, Measure.restrict_apply). For i ≠ i₀ the set {g<3δ} ∩ Π_i is empty and the term is 0; for i = i₀, {g<3δ} ∩ Π_{i₀} = Π_{i₀}. Hence ν⌞{g<3δ}(B) = ofReal(α_{i₀})·Hⁿ(B ∩ Π_{i₀}) for every measurable B (Finset.sum_eq_single), i.e. ν⌞{g<3δ} = ofReal(α_{i₀})·Hⁿ⌞Π_{i₀} (Measure.ext).
6. (Compactness.) K_{t,r} := {g ≤ t} ∩ pL⁻¹(closedBall(0, r)) is closed (g and pL continuous). For x ∈ K_{t,r}, step 1 applied to x − w gives ‖x − w‖² = ‖pL x − pL w‖² + g(x)² ≤ (r + ‖pL w‖)² + max(t, 0)², so K_{t,r} is bounded; ℝ^P is proper, hence K_{t,r} is compact (Metric.isCompact_of_isClosed_isBounded). ∎
proof_key_steps: Q(x) = x − Σ_j⟨v_j,x⟩v_j is the orthogonal projection onto V₀^⊥ and ‖x‖² = ‖pL x‖² + ‖Q x‖².
g(x) := ‖Q(x − w_{i₀})‖ is 1-Lipschitz and equals ‖w_j − w_{i₀}‖ on Π_j.
δ := (1/3)·min(1, min_{j≠i₀}‖w_j − w_{i₀}‖) > 0 separates Π_{i₀} ⊆ {g = 0} from the other planes ⊆ {g ≥ 3δ}.
Hence ν⌞{g<3δ} = ofReal(α_{i₀})Hⁿ⌞Π_{i₀}; {g ≤ t} ∩ pL⁻¹(B̄_r) is closed and bounded, hence compact.

Source: steps 2–4 of the parent proof (slicing by g with L = 1 there, choice of a good level with (MM), convergence of slices with (T2), passage to a subsequence), stated for an abstract L-Lipschitz g, open G, interval (a, b) and limit X.
1. (Slicing each Γ_k.) Fix k. Apply (SL) with ambient P, degree index d (so T ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}), U := ℝ^P (open), T := Γ_k, (μ, ξ) := (μ_k, ξ_k), (μ', ξ') := (0, 0) (the zero measure and the zero field ℝ^P → Λ_d(ℝ^P)), f := g and L. Its hypotheses hold: μ_k is finite on compacts, the zero measure is finite; ξ_k is a.e. strongly measurable and 0 is strongly measurable; the bound for ξ_k holds μ_k-a.e. and every statement holds a.e. for the zero measure; Γ_k(ω) = ∫ξ_k(ω)dμ_k; ∂Γ_k(η) = 0 = ∫ξ'(η)d0 (∂Γ_k = 0, integral_zero_measure); g is L-Lipschitz. For an l-form ω on ℝⁿ write (p^#ω)(x) := ω(pL x)∘pL = (ω(pL x)).compContinuousLinearMap pL ∈ Λ^l(ℝ^P). Then there is Y ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with (i) Y(ω) = ∫_Fξ(x)((p^#ω)(x))dμ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U); (ii) M_U(Y) ≤ μ(F ∩ pL⁻¹(U)); (iii) M_W(∂Y) ≤ M_{pL⁻¹(W)}(∂Z) for every open W ⊆ U; (iv) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) there is a test n-form ω' on ℝ^P with ω'(x) = (p^#ω)(x) for every x ∈ S.

Source: steps 5–7 (and the cutoff used in step 8) of the parent proof, with Y_k = p_#(Γ_k⌞{g<t}) written as an integral; here U = B_{2R}, S = {g ≤ t}, F = {g < t} in the parent. Uses the sibling covector_bounds (b): |γ∘pL| ≤ |γ| for every l-covector γ on ℝⁿ.
0. Tools. (N1) |c·α| = |c|·|α| and |α| ≥ 0 for covectors (each coefficient α(e∘I) scales by c; covectorEuclideanNorm is the square root of the sum of their squares). (N2) |α| ≤ C_l‖α‖ with C_l := (number of strictly increasing I)^{1/2}, because |α(e∘I)| ≤ ‖α‖∏_k‖e_{I(k)}‖ = ‖α‖ (ContinuousMultilinearMap.le_opNorm); also α ↦ |α| is continuous (square root of a finite sum of squares of the continuous linear functionals α ↦ α(e∘I)). (N3) |(p^#γ)(x)| ≤ |γ(pL x)| for every form γ on ℝⁿ (covector_bounds (b)). (N4) Cutoffs: if K ⊆ ℝ^P is compact, O ⊆ ℝ^P open and K ⊆ O, there are r > 0 with cthickening(2r, K) ⊆ O compact (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open, IsCompact.cthickening) and, by exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff (smooth Urysohn in a finite-dimensional space) applied to the open set thickening(2r, K) and the closed set cthickening(r, K) ⊆ thickening(2r, K), a smooth χ : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with support χ = thickening(2r, K) and χ = 1 on cthickening(r, K); then tsupport χ ⊆ cthickening(2r, K) ⊆ O is compact and χ = 1 on the open set O' := thickening(r, K) ⊇ K. (N5) If γ : ℝⁿ → Λ^l(ℝⁿ) is smooth then x ↦ (p^#γ)(x) = (ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMapCLM pL)(γ(pL x)) is smooth (composition with the continuous linear maps pL and compContinuousLinearMapCLM pL), and (p^#γ)(x) = 0 whenever pL x ∉ tsupport γ. (N6) Locality and naturality of d: if two forms agree on a neighbourhood of x their exterior derivatives agree at x (extDeriv ω x = alternatizeUncurryFin (fderiv ℝ ω x) and Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq); for smooth γ on ℝⁿ, d(p^#γ)(x) = (p^#(dγ))(x) for every x (extDeriv_pullback with f := pL, which is smooth with fderiv ℝ pL x = pL).
1. (Integrability.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and K := tsupport ω, compact and ⊆ U. The integrand Φ_ω(x) := ξ(x)((p^#ω)(x)) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (ξ is a.e. strongly measurable into MultiVector P n, x ↦ (p^#ω)(x) is continuous, and the evaluation (ζ, β) ↦ ζ(β) is continuous; AEStronglyMeasurable.prodMk and Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable). For μ-a.e. x: |Φ_ω(x)| ≤ |(p^#ω)(x)| ≤ |ω(pL x)| ≤ ‖ω‖_* := sup_y|ω(y)| < ∞ (N2, N3; y ↦ |ω(y)| is continuous with compact support), and Φ_ω(x) = 0 unless pL x ∈ K (N5). Hence |1_FΦ_ω| ≤ ‖ω‖_*·1_{S ∩ pL⁻¹(K)} μ-a.e. (F ⊆ S) and μ(S ∩ pL⁻¹(K)) < ∞ (compact by hypothesis), so 1_FΦ_ω is μ-integrable.
2. (Linearity.) ω ↦ p^#ω is linear (compContinuousLinearMap is linear in the alternating map) and ξ(x) is linear, so Φ_{aω+bη} = aΦ_ω + bΦ_η and, by step 1, Y₀(ω) := ∫_FΦ_ωdμ is an ℝ-linear functional on 𝒟ⁿ(U) (integral_add, integral_smul).
3. (Continuity.) Let ω_j → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOnConverges): there is a compact K ⊆ U containing every tsupport ω_j, and ω_j → 0 uniformly on K (the k = 0 case: ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω_j x‖ = ‖ω_j x‖, norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero), while ω_j = 0 off K. By step 1 and (N2): |Y₀(ω_j)| ≤ μ(S ∩ pL⁻¹(K))·C_n·sup_{y∈K}‖ω_j(y)‖ → 0. Hence Y := ⟨Y₀, continuity⟩ ∈ 𝒟_n(U), and (i) holds by definition.
4. (Mass, (ii).) Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y. For μ-a.e. x ∈ F: |Φ_ω(x)| ≤ |ω(pL x)| ≤ 1, and Φ_ω(x) = 0 if pL x ∉ U (then pL x ∉ tsupport ω ⊆ U). So Y(ω) ≤ |Y(ω)| ≤ ∫_F1_{pL⁻¹(U)}dμ = μ(F ∩ pL⁻¹(U)) (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le / integral_mono_ae; trivial if the right side is ∞). Thus ofReal(Y ω) ≤ μ(F ∩ pL⁻¹U) for every ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n U, and M_U(Y) ≤ μ(F ∩ pL⁻¹(U)) (sSup_le).
5. (Extension, (iv).) Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), K := S ∩ pL⁻¹(tsupport ω) (compact by hypothesis). Take χ, O' from (N4) with O := ℝ^P and set ω' := χ·p^#ω. By (N5) ω' is smooth with tsupport ω' ⊆ tsupport χ compact, so ω' is a test n-form on ℝ^P. For x ∈ S: if x ∈ O', χ(x) = 1 and ω'(x) = (p^#ω)(x); if x ∉ O' then x ∉ K, so pL x ∉ tsupport ω and (p^#ω)(x) = 0 = ω'(x).
6. (Boundary mass, (iii).) Let W ⊆ U be open and γ ∈ massAdmissibleOn U d W: γ ∈ 𝒟^d(U), tsupport γ ⊆ W, |γ(y)| ≤ 1 for all y. K := S ∩ pL⁻¹(tsupport γ) is compact (hypothesis; tsupport γ is a compact subset of U) and contained in the open set pL⁻¹(W). Take χ, O' from (N4) with O := pL⁻¹(W) and set γ' := χ·p^#γ: a test d-form on ℝ^P (N5) with tsupport γ' ⊆ tsupport χ ⊆ pL⁻¹(W) and |γ'(x)| = χ(x)|(p^#γ)(x)| ≤ |γ(pL x)| ≤ 1 (N1, N3). So γ' ∈ massAdmissibleOn ℝ^P d (pL⁻¹W) and ofReal(∂Z(γ')) ≤ M_{pL⁻¹(W)}(∂Z) (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn). Claim: dγ'(x) = (p^#(dγ))(x) for every x ∈ S. If x ∈ O', γ' = p^#γ on the neighbourhood O' of x, so dγ'(x) = d(p^#γ)(x) = (p^#(dγ))(x) (N6). If x ∈ S ∖ O', then x ∉ K, so pL x ∉ tsupport γ; tsupport γ is closed, so γ = 0 on an open V ∋ pL x; then p^#γ and γ' vanish on the open neighbourhood pL⁻¹(V) of x, so dγ'(x) = 0, and dγ = 0 on V, so (p^#(dγ))(x) = 0 (N6). Now dγ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), dγ' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) (exteriorDerivativeTestOn), F ⊆ S, and by (i), the representation of Z and the claim (setIntegral_congr on F): ∂Y(γ) = Y(dγ) = ∫_Fξ(x)((p^#(dγ))(x))dμ = ∫_Fξ(x)(dγ'(x))dμ = Z(dγ') = ∂Z(γ'). Hence ofReal(∂Y(γ)) ≤ M_{pL⁻¹(W)}(∂Z) for every admissible γ, and M_W(∂Y) ≤ M_{pL⁻¹(W)}(∂Z) (sSup_le). ∎
proof_key_steps: The integrand ξ(x)((p^#ω)(x)) is a.e. bounded by sup|ω| and vanishes off the compact set S ∩ pL⁻¹(spt ω), so Y(ω) := ∫_F ξ(p^#ω)dμ is a continuous linear current on U.
|p^#ω| ≤ |ω∘pL| (covector_bounds) gives M_U(Y) ≤ μ(F ∩ pL⁻¹U).
A smooth cutoff χ ≡ 1 near S ∩ pL⁻¹(spt ω) turns p^#ω into a test form ω' on ℝ^P agreeing with p^#ω on S.
For admissible γ, γ' := χ·p^#γ is admissible for M_{pL⁻¹W}(∂Z) and d γ' = p^#(dγ) on S by locality and naturality of d, so ∂Y(γ) = ∂Z(γ').

subproblems.statement: Hypothesis name: (REP) is the exact frozen statement of cmc_exists_massRepresentation, copied verbatim as the first hypothesis of the Lean statement. In words: for P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open and T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with M_W(T) < ∞ for every open W ⊂⊂ U there are a Borel measure μ and ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) with μ(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0, μ(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U, μ(W) = M_W(T) for every open W, ξ μ-a.e. strongly measurable, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x and α, T(ω) = ∫ξ(x)(ω(x))dμ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), and, provided also boundaryMassOn T W < ∞ (i.e. M_W(∂T) < ∞ in positive degree) for every open W ⊂⊂ U, μ(E) = 0 whenever Hⁿ(E) = 0. Assume (REP). Let d ∈ ℕ, n := d + 1, U ⊆ ℝⁿ open and Y ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with M_U(Y) < ∞ and M_W(∂Y) < ∞ for every open W ⊂⊂ U (closure W compact and contained in U). Then there is u : ℝⁿ → ℝ, Lebesgue integrable on U, with ofReal(∫_U|u|dy) ≤ M_U(Y) and Y(ω) = ∫_U u(y)·ω(y)(e_0, …, e_d)dy for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), where e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1.
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsOpen U → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → T.massOn W < ∞) → ∃ (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P n), μ Uᶜ = 0 ∧ (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ K < ∞) ∧ (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → T.massOn W = μ W) ∧ AEStronglyMeasurable ξ μ ∧ (∀ (x : Euclid P) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), |ξ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) ∧ (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, T ω = ∫ x, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ∂μ) ∧ ((∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → boundaryMassOn T W < ∞) → ∀ E : Set (Euclid P), μHE[n] E = 0 → μ E = 0)) → ∀ (d : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid (d + 1))) (Y : GeometricCurrentOn U (d + 1)), IsOpen U → Y.massOn U < ∞ → (∀ W : Set (Euclid (d + 1)), IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → Y.boundary.massOn W < ∞) → ∃ u : Euclid (d + 1) → ℝ, IntegrableOn u U ∧ ENNReal.ofReal (∫ y in U, |u y|) ≤ Y.massOn U ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn U (d + 1), Y ω = ∫ y in U, u y * (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid (d + 1)) (d + 1)) y (fun i => EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 9 of the parent proof (densities of Y_k from (REP), absolute continuity, Lebesgue decomposition, u_k := ρ_k·ξ_{Y_k}(dy)).
1. (Applying (REP).) For every open W ⊂⊂ U we have W ⊆ closure W ⊆ U, so M_W(Y) ≤ M_U(Y) < ∞ (GeometricCurrentOn.massOn_mono). Apply (REP) with ambient dimension P := n, degree n, U and T := Y; obtain μ and ξ with μ(ℝⁿ ∖ U) = 0, μ(W) = M_W(Y) for every open W, ξ μ-a.e. strongly measurable, |ξ(y)(α)| ≤ |α| for all y, α, Y(ω) = ∫ξ(y)(ω(y))dμ(y) for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), and the boundary clause. For degree n = d + 1, boundaryMassOn Y W is by definition Y.boundary.massOn W (rfl), which is finite for every open W ⊂⊂ U by hypothesis; hence μ(E) = 0 whenever μHE[n](E) = 0.
2. (Finiteness.) ℝⁿ is open, so μ(ℝⁿ) = M_{ℝⁿ}(Y); and M_{ℝⁿ}(Y) = M_U(Y) because every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) already has tsupport ω ⊆ U, so massAdmissibleOn U n ℝⁿ = massAdmissibleOn U n U. Thus μ(ℝⁿ) = M_U(Y) < ∞ and μ is a finite measure.
3. (Absolute continuity.) μHE[n] = volume on Euclid n (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume), so μ ≪ volume.
4. (Radon–Nikodym density.) Let ρ := μ.rnDeriv volume (measurable, Measure.measurable_rnDeriv). By the Lebesgue decomposition (Measure.haveLebesgueDecomposition_add: μ = μ.singularPart volume + volume.withDensity ρ, available since μ is finite and volume σ-finite) and Measure.singularPart_eq_zero_of_ac (μ ≪ volume) we get μ = volume.withDensity ρ. Hence ∫⁻ρ = μ(ℝⁿ) < ∞, ρ < ∞ a.e., and y ↦ ρ(y).toReal is integrable with ∫ρ.toReal = μ(ℝⁿ).toReal = M_U(Y).toReal (integral_toReal).
5. (The top covector dy.) Let dy ∈ Λⁿ(ℝⁿ) be the determinant with respect to the standard basis: dy(u) := det(Matrix.of fun i j => (u j) i), i.e. the alternating map (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ).toBasis.det, which is continuous because u ↦ det(…) is continuous (Continuous.matrix_det), hence a ContinuousAlternatingMap; dy(e_0, …, e_d) = 1 (Basis.det_self). The only strictly increasing I : Fin n → Fin n is the identity, so |dy|² = dy(e)² = 1. Every λ ∈ Λⁿ(ℝⁿ) satisfies λ = λ(e)·dy (AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det for the standard basis, applied to the underlying alternating maps), hence for every y and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U): ξ(y)(ω(y)) = ω(y)(e)·ξ(y)(dy).
6. (Definition of u.) Choose a strongly measurable ξ̃ with ξ = ξ̃ μ-a.e. (AEStronglyMeasurable.mk). Put h(y) := ξ̃(y)(dy) (strongly measurable; evaluation at the fixed dy is a continuous linear functional) and u(y) := ρ(y).toReal·h(y). Since |ξ(y)(dy)| ≤ |dy| = 1 for all y, |h| ≤ 1 μ-a.e.; by ae_withDensity_iff (μ = volume.withDensity ρ) this means: for volume-a.e. y, ρ(y) ≠ 0 ⇒ |h(y)| ≤ 1. Hence |u(y)| ≤ ρ(y).toReal for volume-a.e. y (both sides vanish where ρ(y) = 0). So u is integrable on ℝⁿ (strongly measurable, dominated by the integrable ρ.toReal), in particular on U, and ∫_U|u| ≤ ∫|u| ≤ ∫ρ.toReal = M_U(Y).toReal, whence ofReal(∫_U|u|) ≤ M_U(Y) (ENNReal.ofReal_le_of_le_toReal, M_U(Y) < ∞).
7. (Representation.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). By step 5 and ξ = ξ̃ μ-a.e., Y(ω) = ∫ξ(y)(ω(y))dμ = ∫ω(y)(e)·h(y)dμ(y). By integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul (ρ measurable, ρ < ∞ a.e.): ∫ω(y)(e)h(y)d(volume.withDensity ρ) = ∫ρ(y).toReal·ω(y)(e)h(y)dy = ∫u(y)ω(y)(e)dy. Finally ω(y) = 0 for y ∉ U (tsupport ω ⊆ U), so the integrand vanishes off U and ∫u(y)ω(y)(e)dy = ∫_U u(y)ω(y)(e)dy (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero). ∎
proof_key_steps: (REP) applied to Y on U gives (μ, ξ) with μ(W) = M_W(Y) and, by the finite boundary mass, μ ≪ Hⁿ = Lⁿ.
μ(ℝⁿ) = M_U(Y) < ∞, so μ = ρLⁿ with ρ = rnDeriv (Lebesgue decomposition, zero singular part).
Every top covector is λ(e)·dy, so Y(ω) = ∫ω(e)ξ(dy)dμ = ∫ρ.toReal·ξ̃(dy)·ω(e)dy.
u := ρ.toReal·ξ̃(dy) satisfies |u| ≤ ρ.toReal a.e., hence ∫_U|u| ≤ M_U(Y), and Y(ω) = ∫_U u·ω(e).

0. (Measurable versions.) Choose a measurable ũ with u = ũ volume-a.e. on U (IntegrableOn gives AEStronglyMeasurable for volume⌞U; AEStronglyMeasurable.mk) and a measurable h̃ with h = h̃ σ-a.e. The hypothesis holds with (ũ, h̃) in place of (u, h) (integrals of a.e.-equal functions agree), ũ is integrable on U and h̃ is σ-integrable; and B ∩ {u ≠ 0} ⊆ (B ∩ {ũ ≠ 0}) ∪ (U ∩ {u ≠ ũ}) with the last set volume-null, so the conclusion for ũ implies it for u (measure_union_le). Hence we may and do assume that u and h are measurable.
1. (Finite measures.) Let u^± := max(±u, 0), h^± := max(±h, 0) (measurable, nonnegative). Put λ_± := (volume⌞U).withDensity(ofReal∘u^±) and m_± := Measure.map q (σ.withDensity(ofReal∘h^±)) (q is continuous, hence measurable). They are finite: λ_±(ℝⁿ) = ∫⁻_U ofReal(u^±) ≤ ∫⁻_U ofReal|u| < ∞ and m_±(ℝⁿ) = ∫⁻ofReal(h^±)dσ < ∞. Set σ₁ := (λ₊ + m₋)⌞U and σ₂ := (λ₋ + m₊)⌞U, finite Borel measures on ℝⁿ.
2. (Equal integrals of test functions.) Let b be smooth, compactly supported, tsupport b ⊆ U; b is bounded, continuous and vanishes off U. Then ∫b dσ₁ = ∫_U b u⁺ + ∫b(q x)h⁻(x)dσ(x): restricting to U does not change the integral of b (b = 0 off U; setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero), integral_add_measure splits the sum, integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul (measurable densities, finite a.e.) gives ∫b dλ₊ = ∫_U u⁺b, and integral_map with the same lemma gives ∫b dm₋ = ∫b(q x)h⁻(x)dσ(x); likewise ∫b dσ₂ = ∫_U b u⁻ + ∫b(q x)h⁺(x)dσ(x). All these integrals are finite (b bounded). Their difference is ∫_U b u − ∫b(q x)h(x)dσ(x) = 0 by hypothesis (u = u⁺ − u⁻, h = h⁺ − h⁻). So ∫b dσ₁ = ∫b dσ₂.
3. (Open sets.) Let O ⊆ ℝⁿ be open and V := O ∩ U (open). For j ∈ ℕ let K_j := {y : infEdist(y, ℝⁿ ∖ V) ≥ 1/(j+1)} ∩ closedBall(0, j): it is closed (infEdist is continuous) and bounded, hence compact, and K_j ⊆ V (points of ℝⁿ ∖ V have infEdist 0; if V = ℝⁿ the infEdist to ∅ is ∞ and K_j = closedBall(0, j)); every y ∈ V lies in K_j for all large j (V open, so infEdist(y, ℝⁿ ∖ V) > 0). Smooth cutoff: choose r_j > 0 with cthickening(2r_j, K_j) ⊆ V (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open); cthickening(2r_j, K_j) is compact (IsCompact.cthickening). Apply exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff (smooth Urysohn in the finite-dimensional space ℝⁿ) to the open set thickening(2r_j, K_j) and the closed set cthickening(r_j, K_j) ⊆ thickening(2r_j, K_j): it gives a smooth b_j : ℝⁿ → [0, 1] with support b_j = thickening(2r_j, K_j) and b_j = 1 on cthickening(r_j, K_j) ⊇ K_j; so tsupport b_j ⊆ cthickening(2r_j, K_j) ⊆ V ⊆ U is compact. Then b_j(y) → 1_V(y) for every y, |b_j| ≤ 1, and σ_i is finite, so by dominated convergence (tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence with the constant bound 1) ∫b_j dσ_i → σ_i(V) = σ_i(O) (σ_i is carried by U). By step 2, σ₁(O) = σ₂(O) for every open O.
4. (Uniqueness.) The open sets form a π-system (isPiSystem_isOpen) generating the Borel σ-algebra of ℝⁿ (borel = generateFrom {open}; BorelSpace.measurable_eq), ℝⁿ is open and σ₁, σ₂ are finite; so σ₁ = σ₂ (MeasureTheory.ext_of_generate_finite). In particular (λ₊ + m₋)(B') = (λ₋ + m₊)(B') for every measurable B' ⊆ U.
5. (Measurable hull.) Let E := toMeasurable volume (q(A)), a measurable superset of q(A) with volume(E ∩ B) = volume(q(A) ∩ B) for every measurable B (Measure.measure_toMeasurable_inter_of_sFinite; volume is σ-finite). Let B' ⊆ U ∖ E be measurable. If x ∈ A and q(x) ∈ B', then q(x) ∈ q(A) ⊆ E, impossible; so q⁻¹(B') ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ A, σ(q⁻¹(B')) = 0, and m_±(B') = ∫⁻_{q⁻¹(B')}ofReal(h^±)dσ = 0 (Measure.map_apply, withDensity_apply, setLIntegral_measure_zero). By step 4, λ₊(B') = λ₋(B'), i.e. ∫⁻_{B'}ofReal(u⁺) = ∫⁻_{B'}ofReal(u⁻).
6. (Vanishing off E.) Apply step 5 to B'₊ := (U ∖ E) ∩ {u > 0} (measurable): u⁻ = 0 on B'₊, so ∫⁻_{B'₊}ofReal(u⁺) = 0, hence u⁺ = 0 a.e. on B'₊ (setLIntegral_eq_zero_iff / lintegral_eq_zero_iff); but u⁺ = u > 0 on B'₊, so volume(B'₊) = 0. Symmetrically volume((U ∖ E) ∩ {u < 0}) = 0. Hence volume((U ∖ E) ∩ {u ≠ 0}) = 0.
7. (Conclusion.) For measurable B ⊆ U: B ∩ {u ≠ 0} ⊆ (E ∩ B) ∪ ((U ∖ E) ∩ {u ≠ 0}), so volume(B ∩ {u ≠ 0}) ≤ volume(E ∩ B) + 0 = volume(q(A) ∩ B) = volume(B ∩ q(A)) (measure_union_le and the hull identity of step 5). ∎

Smooth cutoffs b_j ↑ 1_{O∩U} and dominated convergence give σ₁ = σ₂ on open sets, hence on all Borel sets (π-system uniqueness).
For Borel B' ⊆ U ∖ toMeasurable(q(A)), q⁻¹(B') is σ-null, so ∫_{B'}u⁺ = ∫_{B'}u⁻ and u = 0 a.e. on U ∖ E.
Lⁿ(B ∩ {u ≠ 0}) ≤ Lⁿ(E ∩ B) = Lⁿ(q(A) ∩ B) by the hull property.

subproblems.title: The d-form f·ι_z(dy) on ℝ^{d+1} has exterior derivative (∂_z f)·dy
subproblems.statement: Let d ∈ ℕ and z ∈ ℝ^{d+1} = Euclid (d+1). There is a d-covector ε on ℝ^{d+1} with |ε| ≤ ‖z‖ (|·| = covectorEuclideanNorm) such that for every f : ℝ^{d+1} → ℝ and every y at which f is differentiable, the exterior derivative of the d-form x ↦ f(x)·ε satisfies d(f·ε)(y)(e_0, …, e_d) = Df(y)(z), where e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (d : ℕ) (z : Euclid (d + 1)), ∃ ε : Covector (Euclid (d + 1)) d, covectorEuclideanNorm ε ≤ ‖z‖ ∧ ∀ (f : Euclid (d + 1) → ℝ) (y : Euclid (d + 1)), DifferentiableAt ℝ f y → exteriorDerivative (fun x => f x • ε) y (fun i => EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)) = fderiv ℝ f y z
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 11(b) of the parent proof (with ε_j := (−1)^{j−1}dy¹∧⋯∧dy^{j−1}∧dy^{j+1}∧⋯∧dyⁿ, (∇f·z)dy = d(f·Σ_j z_jε_j) and |Σ_j z_jε_j| ≤ |z|); here ε = Σ_j z_jε_j is written as the interior product ι_z(dy), ε(u_1, …, u_d) = det[z | u_1 | ⋯ | u_d].
1. (Definition.) For u : Fin d → ℝ^{d+1} let M(u) be the (d+1)×(d+1) matrix whose column 0 is z and whose column k+1 is u_k, i.e. M(u)_{r,c} := (Fin.cons z u : Fin (d+1) → ℝ^{d+1}) c r, and ε(u) := det M(u). Equivalently ε(u) = D(Fin.cons z u) with D the determinant alternating map of the standard basis ((EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin (d+1)) ℝ).toBasis.det), i.e. ε is the curried map D.curryLeft z (AlternatingMap.curryLeft). It is multilinear and alternating in u (det is multilinear and alternating in the columns) and continuous (u ↦ det M(u) is continuous, Continuous.matrix_det), so ε ∈ Covector (Euclid (d+1)) d.
2. (Values on coordinate tuples.) Let i ∈ Fin (d+1) and u := i.removeNth e = (e_{i.succAbove k})_{k ∈ Fin d}. Expanding det M(u) along column 0 (Matrix.det_succ_column_zero): det M(u) = Σ_{r ∈ Fin (d+1)} (−1)^r z_r det N_r, where N_r is the d×d matrix with entries (N_r)_{a,k} = (e_{i.succAbove k})_{r.succAbove a} = δ_{r.succAbove a, i.succAbove k}. For r = i, N_i is the identity (succAbove is injective), det = 1. For r ≠ i, i = r.succAbove a₀ for some a₀ (Fin.exists_succAbove_eq) and row a₀ of N_r is zero (i is not in the range of i.succAbove), so det N_r = 0 (Matrix.det_eq_zero_of_row_eq_zero). Hence ε(i.removeNth e) = (−1)^i z_i.
3. (Norm.) The strictly increasing maps I : Fin d → Fin (d+1) are exactly I = i.succAbove for i ∈ Fin (d+1) (a strictly increasing map omits exactly one value i — its range has d elements — and is then the increasing enumeration of the complement of {i}, which is i.succAbove; StrictMono.range_inj / Fin.succAbove range, Finset.orderEmbOfFin_unique), and i ↦ i.succAbove is injective. Using step 2 (i.succAbove composed with e is i.removeNth e): |ε|² = Σ_{I strictly increasing} ε(e∘I)² = Σ_{i ∈ Fin (d+1)} ((−1)^i z_i)² = Σ_i z_i² = ‖z‖² (EuclideanSpace.norm_eq, Real.sq_sqrt), so |ε| = ‖z‖ ≤ ‖z‖. (For the inequality it also suffices to bound the finite sum over strictly increasing I by the sum over the image of i ↦ i.succAbove.)
4. (Exterior derivative.) Let ω(x) := f(x)·ε. If f is differentiable at y, so is ω (product of a differentiable scalar function and a constant vector), and exteriorDerivative_apply / extDeriv_apply with v := e gives dω(y)(e) = Σ_{i ∈ Fin (d+1)} (−1)^i·D[x ↦ ω(x)(i.removeNth e)](y)(e_i). Here ω(x)(i.removeNth e) = f(x)·ε(i.removeNth e) = (−1)^i z_i f(x), whose derivative at y is (−1)^i z_i Df(y) (fderiv_mul_const). So dω(y)(e) = Σ_i (−1)^i(−1)^i z_i Df(y)(e_i) = Σ_i z_i Df(y)(e_i) = Df(y)(Σ_i z_i e_i) = Df(y)(z) ((−1)^i(−1)^i = 1; z = Σ_i z_i e_i in Euclid (d+1), EuclideanSpace.basisFun / PiLp sum decomposition; linearity of Df(y)). ∎
proof_key_steps: Define ε(u) := det[z | u_1 | ⋯ | u_d] (curryLeft of the standard determinant); it is a continuous alternating d-form.
Laplace expansion along the first column gives ε(i.removeNth e) = (−1)^i z_i.
Strictly increasing I are exactly i.succAbove, so |ε|² = Σ_i z_i² = ‖z‖².
extDeriv_apply: d(fε)(y)(e) = Σ_i (−1)^i(−1)^i z_i ∂_if(y) = Df(y)(z).

subproblems.title: Mollifications of weakly converging, L¹-bounded densities converge uniformly on a smaller ball
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, R > 0, 0 < s < R, c, Λ ∈ ℝ, φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ smooth (ContDiff ℝ ⊤) with tsupport φ ⊆ B_s(0), and u_k : ℝⁿ → ℝ (k ∈ ℕ) Lebesgue integrable on B_{2R}(0) with ∫_{B_{2R}(0)}|u_k| ≤ Λ for all sufficiently large k. Assume ∫_{B_{2R}(0)}u_k b → c∫_{ℝⁿ}b for every smooth compactly supported b with tsupport b ⊆ B_{2R}(0). Then w_k(x) := ∫_{B_{2R}(0)}u_k(y)φ(x − y)dy converges to c∫_{ℝⁿ}φ uniformly on closedBall(0, R).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (R s c Λ : ℝ) (φ : Euclid n → ℝ) (u : ℕ → Euclid n → ℝ), 0 < R → 0 < s → s < R → ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) φ → tsupport φ ⊆ ball 0 s → (∀ k, IntegrableOn (u k) (ball 0 (2 * R))) → (∀ᶠ k in atTop, ∫ y in ball 0 (2 * R), |u k y| ≤ Λ) → (∀ b : Euclid n → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) b → HasCompactSupport b → tsupport b ⊆ ball 0 (2 * R) → Tendsto (fun k => ∫ y in ball 0 (2 * R), u k y * b y) atTop (𝓝 (c * ∫ y, b y))) → TendstoUniformlyOn (fun k x => ∫ y in ball 0 (2 * R), u k y * φ (x - y)) (fun _ => c * ∫ y, φ y) atTop (closedBall 0 R)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 11(a) of the parent proof ((u_k∗φ_{s₀})(x) = Y_k(φ_{s₀}(x − ·)dy) → θ₀α pointwise, equi-Lipschitz with constant Λ·Lip(φ_{s₀}), hence uniformly on the compact B̄_R).
1. (Regularity of φ.) tsupport φ ⊆ B_s(0) is closed and bounded, hence compact, so φ has compact support; φ is C¹, hence Lipschitz with some constant L_φ ≥ 0 (ContDiff.lipschitzWith_of_hasCompactSupport).
2. (Pointwise convergence.) Fix x ∈ closedBall(0, R) and b_x(y) := φ(x − y). b_x is smooth (composition with the affine map y ↦ x − y) and tsupport b_x = x − tsupport φ ⊆ {x − z : ‖z‖ < s} = B_s(x) ⊆ B_{R+s}(0) ⊆ B_{2R}(0) because s < R; it is compact (image of a compact set under a homeomorphism). Moreover ∫b_x = ∫φ(x − y)dy = ∫φ (integral_sub_left_eq_self: volume on Euclid n is an additive Haar measure, invariant under y ↦ x − y). By hypothesis w_k(x) = ∫_{B_{2R}}u_k b_x → c∫b_x = c∫φ.
3. (Equi-Lipschitz.) Let k be large enough that ∫_{B_{2R}}|u_k| ≤ Λ (then Λ ≥ 0). For all x, x': |w_k(x) − w_k(x')| ≤ ∫_{B_{2R}}|u_k(y)||φ(x − y) − φ(x' − y)|dy ≤ L_φ‖x − x'‖∫_{B_{2R}}|u_k| ≤ L_φΛ‖x − x'‖ (integral_sub, norm_integral_le_integral_norm, integral_mono with the Lipschitz bound; the integrands are integrable since u_k is integrable on B_{2R} and φ is bounded).
4. (Uniformity.) Let ε > 0 and η > 0 with (L_φ max(Λ, 0) + 1)η < ε/3. closedBall(0, R) is compact, so there are x_1, …, x_m ∈ closedBall(0, R) whose η-balls cover it (IsCompact.finite_cover_balls / totally bounded). By step 2 choose k₁ with |w_k(x_i) − c∫φ| < ε/3 for all i and k ≥ k₁, and by hypothesis k₂ such that the Λ-bound holds for k ≥ k₂. For k ≥ max(k₁, k₂) and x ∈ closedBall(0, R) pick i with ‖x − x_i‖ < η; by step 3, |w_k(x) − c∫φ| ≤ |w_k(x) − w_k(x_i)| + |w_k(x_i) − c∫φ| < ε/3 + ε/3 < ε. This is TendstoUniformlyOn (Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff) of w_k to the constant c∫φ on closedBall(0, R). ∎
proof_key_steps: φ has compact support and is Lipschitz.
For x ∈ B̄_R, b_x = φ(x − ·) is a test function in B_{2R} with ∫b_x = ∫φ, so w_k(x) → c∫φ.
The w_k are eventually equi-Lipschitz with constant L_φΛ.
Pointwise convergence on a finite η-net of the compact B̄_R plus equicontinuity gives uniform convergence.

subproblems.title: L¹ mollification error is at most s times the variation bound
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, R > 0, s > 0 with 2s < R, V ≥ 0, φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ smooth with φ ≥ 0, tsupport φ ⊆ B_s(0) and ∫φ = 1, and u : ℝⁿ → ℝ Lebesgue integrable on B_{2R}(0). Assume |∫_{B_{2R}(0)}u(y)·Df(y)(z)dy| ≤ V‖z‖M for every smooth compactly supported f : ℝⁿ → ℝ with tsupport f ⊆ B_{2R}(0), every z ∈ ℝⁿ and every M ∈ ℝ with |f| ≤ M everywhere. Then ∫_{B_R(0)}|u(x) − w(x)|dx ≤ sV, where w(x) := ∫_{B_{2R}(0)}u(y)φ(x − y)dy.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (R s V : ℝ) (φ u : Euclid n → ℝ), 0 < R → 0 < s → 2 * s < R → 0 ≤ V → ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) φ → (∀ y, 0 ≤ φ y) → tsupport φ ⊆ ball 0 s → ∫ y, φ y = 1 → IntegrableOn u (ball 0 (2 * R)) → (∀ (f : Euclid n → ℝ) (z : Euclid n) (M : ℝ), ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) f → HasCompactSupport f → tsupport f ⊆ ball 0 (2 * R) → (∀ y, |f y| ≤ M) → |∫ y in ball 0 (2 * R), u y * fderiv ℝ f y z| ≤ V * ‖z‖ * M) → ∫ x in ball 0 R, |u x - ∫ y in ball 0 (2 * R), u y * φ (x - y)| ≤ s * V
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 11(b) of the parent proof (the BV estimate ∫_{B_R}|u_k − u_k∗φ_{s₀}| ≤ s₀M_{B_{2R}}(∂Y_k) by duality: h_ϑ = g_ϑ − φ̌∗g_ϑ, the fundamental theorem of calculus along segments, Fubini, and g_ϑ → g at Lebesgue points), with the current hypothesis replaced by the variation bound V.
Notation: ū := u·1_{B_{2R}} ∈ L¹(ℝⁿ), so w(x) = ∫ū(y)φ(x − y)dy; |w| ≤ sup|φ|·‖ū‖₁ and w is continuous (dominated convergence, φ continuous and bounded). If n = 0, ℝ⁰ is a point, volume is the Dirac mass, ∫φ = φ(0) = 1, w(0) = u(0) and the claim is 0 ≤ sV; assume n ≥ 1 if a lemma below needs it.
1. (Claim A: smooth test functions.) Let g : ℝⁿ → ℝ be smooth with |g| ≤ 1 and tsupport g ⊆ closedBall(0, R + s) (so g has compact support). Then |∫(ū − w)g| ≤ sV.
(a) Fubini: the function (x, y) ↦ ū(y)φ(x − y)g(x) is integrable on ℝⁿ × ℝⁿ (bounded by sup|φ|·|ū(y)|·1_{‖x−y‖<s}), so ∫w g = ∫ū(y)(∫φ(x − y)g(x)dx)dy = ∫ū(y)(∫φ(z)g(y + z)dz)dy (integral_integral_swap; translation x = y + z, integral_add_left_eq_self). Using ∫φ = 1, ∫(ū − w)g = ∫ū(y)H(y)dy with H(y) := ∫φ(z)(g(y) − g(y + z))dz.
(b) Fundamental theorem of calculus: for all y, z, g(y) − g(y + z) = −∫_0^1Dg(y + τz)(z)dτ (intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt / integral_unitInterval_deriv_eq_sub for τ ↦ g(y + τz), whose derivative is Dg(y + τz)(z)). So H(y) = −∫φ(z)∫_0^1Dg(y + τz)(z)dτdz.
(c) Fubini again (on ℝⁿ_y × ℝⁿ_z × [0, 1]; the integrand ū(y)φ(z)Dg(y + τz)(z) is bounded by |ū(y)|·φ(z)·s·sup‖Dg‖, integrable): ∫ūH = −∫φ(z)∫_0^1[∫ū(y)Dg(y + τz)(z)dy]dτdz.
(d) For fixed z with φ(z) ≠ 0 (so ‖z‖ < s) and τ ∈ [0, 1], f_{τ,z}(y) := g(y + τz) is smooth, compactly supported, |f_{τ,z}| ≤ 1, Df_{τ,z}(y) = Dg(y + τz), and tsupport f_{τ,z} = tsupport g − τz ⊆ closedBall(0, R + s) + B_s(0) ⊆ B_{R+2s}(0) ⊆ B_{2R}(0) (2s < R). Since ū = u on B_{2R}(0), ∫ū(y)Dg(y + τz)(z)dy = ∫_{B_{2R}}u(y)Df_{τ,z}(y)(z)dy, of absolute value ≤ V‖z‖·1 by hypothesis (M := 1).
(e) Hence |∫(ū − w)g| = |∫ūH| ≤ ∫φ(z)∫_0^1V‖z‖dτdz = V∫φ(z)‖z‖dz ≤ Vs∫φ = sV (φ ≥ 0 and φ(z) = 0 unless ‖z‖ < s).
2. (Smoothing the sign function.) Let ũ be a Borel function with ũ = ū a.e. and put g₀ := sign(ũ − w)·1_{B_R(0)}: Borel, |g₀| ≤ 1, g₀ = 0 off B_R(0), and (ū − w)g₀ = |u − w|·1_{B_R(0)} a.e. Fix a smooth ψ ≥ 0 with tsupport ψ ⊆ B_1(0) and ∫ψ = 1 (a ContDiffBump centred at 0 with rIn = 1/4, rOut = 1/2, divided by its positive integral; it is ≥ 0, smooth, equal to 1 near 0, with tsupport = closedBall(0, 1/2)). For 0 < ϑ < s let ψ_ϑ(x) := ϑ^{−n}ψ(x/ϑ) (smooth, ≥ 0, tsupport ⊆ closedBall(0, ϑ/2), ∫ψ_ϑ = 1 by Measure.integral_comp_inv_smul / the scaling of Lebesgue measure) and g_ϑ(x) := ∫g₀(y)ψ_ϑ(x − y)dy = (g₀ ⋆ ψ_ϑ)(x). Then g_ϑ is smooth (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_right; g₀ is bounded with compact support, hence locally integrable), |g_ϑ| ≤ ∫ψ_ϑ = 1 and tsupport g_ϑ ⊆ closedBall(0, R + ϑ) ⊆ closedBall(0, R + s). By Claim A, |∫(ū − w)g_ϑ| ≤ sV for every ϑ ∈ (0, s).
3. (Lebesgue points.) For a.e. x, g_ϑ(x) → g₀(x) as ϑ → 0+: |g_ϑ(x) − g₀(x)| = |∫ψ_ϑ(x − y)(g₀(y) − g₀(x))dy| ≤ sup ψ·ϑ^{−n}∫_{closedBall(x, ϑ)}|g₀(y) − g₀(x)|dy = sup ψ·volume(closedBall(0, 1))·⨍_{closedBall(x, ϑ)}|g₀ − g₀(x)| (Measure.addHaar_closedBall), and the average tends to 0 at every Lebesgue point of the bounded, locally integrable g₀, i.e. for a.e. x (Lebesgue differentiation theorem: IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure.ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub for the doubling measure volume, or VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub for Besicovitch.vitaliFamily).
4. (Passage to the limit.) Let ϑ_j := s/(j + 2) → 0. The functions (ū − w)g_{ϑ_j} are dominated by |ū − w|·1_{closedBall(0, R+s)}, which is integrable (ū ∈ L¹, w bounded, finite-measure ball), and converge a.e. to (ū − w)g₀ by step 3. By dominated convergence ∫(ū − w)g_{ϑ_j} → ∫(ū − w)g₀ = ∫_{B_R(0)}|u − w|. Since each |∫(ū − w)g_{ϑ_j}| ≤ sV (step 2), ∫_{B_R(0)}|u − w| ≤ sV. ∎
proof_key_steps: For smooth g with |g| ≤ 1 supported in B̄_{R+s}: ∫(ū − w)g = ∫ū(y)∫φ(z)(g(y) − g(y+z))dzdy by Fubini and ∫φ = 1.
FTC along segments and Fubini turn this into −∫φ(z)∫_0^1∫u·D[g(·+τz)](z) dydτdz, bounded by V∫φ(z)|z|dz ≤ sV.
Smooth g₀ = sign(u − w)1_{B_R} by mollification: |g_ϑ| ≤ 1, supports in B̄_{R+s}, and g_ϑ → g₀ a.e. (Lebesgue points).
Dominated convergence gives ∫_{B_R}|u − w| = lim ∫(ū − w)g_ϑ ≤ sV.

subproblems.title: Densities of top-dimensional currents with vanishing boundary mass and constant weak limit converge in L¹
subproblems.statement: Let d ∈ ℕ, n := d + 1, R > 0, c, Λ ∈ ℝ, U := B_{2R}(0) ⊆ ℝⁿ, Y_k ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and u_k : ℝⁿ → ℝ (k ∈ ℕ) with u_k Lebesgue integrable on U, ∫_U|u_k| ≤ Λ for all sufficiently large k, and Y_k(ω) = ∫_U u_k(y)·ω(y)(e_0, …, e_d)dy for every k and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1). Assume M_U(∂Y_k) → 0 and Y_k(ω) → c∫_{ℝⁿ}ω(y)(e_0, …, e_d)dy for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Then ∫_{B_R(0)}|u_k − c| → 0.

Source: step 11 of the parent proof ((a) uniform convergence of u_k∗φ_{s₀}, (b) the BV estimate with the forms ε_j, (c) the combination). Uses the siblings interior_form, mollified_uniform and bv_estimate.
1. (Test functions as top forms.) Let dy ∈ Λⁿ(ℝⁿ) be the determinant of the standard basis (the alternating map (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ).toBasis.det, continuous by Continuous.matrix_det, hence a ContinuousAlternatingMap), so dy(e) = 1. For b smooth with compact support and tsupport b ⊆ U, ω_b(y) := b(y)·dy is a test n-form on U (smooth, compact support, tsupport ω_b ⊆ tsupport b ⊆ U) with ω_b(y)(e) = b(y). Hence ∫_U u_k b = Y_k(ω_b) → c∫b.
2. (Mollifier.) Put s := R/4 (so 0 < s < R and 2s < R). Let φ ≥ 0 be smooth with tsupport φ ⊆ B_s(0) and ∫φ = 1: a ContDiffBump centred at 0 with rIn = s/4, rOut = s/2 (smooth, values in [0, 1], equal to 1 on closedBall(0, s/4), tsupport = closedBall(0, s/2)) divided by its integral, which is positive (continuous, ≥ 0 and = 1 on a ball of positive measure; integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg).
3. (Uniform convergence of the mollifications.) By mollified_uniform (n, R, s, c, Λ, φ, u_k; s < R; integrability and the eventual Λ-bound; step 1), w_k(x) := ∫_U u_k(y)φ(x − y)dy → c∫φ = c uniformly on closedBall(0, R).
4. (Variation bound.) Let V_k := (M_U(∂Y_k)).toReal ≥ 0. As M_U(∂Y_k) → 0 there is k₀ with M_U(∂Y_k) < ∞ for k ≥ k₀, and V_k → 0 (ENNReal.tendsto_toReal at 0). Claim: for k ≥ k₀, every smooth compactly supported f with tsupport f ⊆ U, every z ∈ ℝⁿ and every M with |f| ≤ M: |∫_U u_k(y)Df(y)(z)dy| ≤ V_k‖z‖M. Proof: by interior_form take ε_z ∈ Λ^d(ℝⁿ) with |ε_z| ≤ ‖z‖ and d(f·ε_z)(y)(e) = Df(y)(z) for every y (f is differentiable everywhere). γ := f·ε_z is a test d-form on U (smooth, tsupport γ ⊆ tsupport f ⊆ U), and dγ is a test n-form on U (exteriorDerivativeTestOn), so by the representation of Y_k: ∂Y_k(γ) = Y_k(dγ) = ∫_U u_k(y)dγ(y)(e)dy = ∫_U u_k(y)Df(y)(z)dy. Pointwise |γ(y)| = |f(y)|·|ε_z| ≤ M‖z‖ (covectorEuclideanNorm (a·α) = |a|·|α|; M ≥ 0 since |f| ≤ M). For every η > 0 the forms ±(M‖z‖ + η)⁻¹γ have coefficient norm ≤ 1 and tsupport ⊆ U, so they belong to massAdmissibleOn U d U and ofReal(±(M‖z‖ + η)⁻¹∂Y_k(γ)) ≤ M_U(∂Y_k) (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn, linearity of ∂Y_k); since M_U(∂Y_k) < ∞ this gives |∂Y_k(γ)| ≤ (M‖z‖ + η)V_k, and letting η → 0, |∂Y_k(γ)| ≤ V_k‖z‖M.
5. (BV estimate.) For k ≥ k₀, bv_estimate (n, R, s, V_k, φ, u_k; 2s < R, V_k ≥ 0, φ ≥ 0, tsupport φ ⊆ B_s(0), ∫φ = 1, u_k integrable on U, step 4) gives ∫_{B_R}|u_k − w_k| ≤ sV_k.
6. (Conclusion.) For k ≥ k₀: |u_k − c| ≤ |u_k − w_k| + |w_k − c| pointwise, all functions involved are integrable on B_R(0) (u_k ∈ L¹(B_R), w_k continuous hence bounded on the bounded ball), so ∫_{B_R}|u_k − c| ≤ ∫_{B_R}|u_k − w_k| + ∫_{B_R}|w_k − c| ≤ sV_k + volume(B_R(0)).toReal·sup_{x ∈ closedBall(0,R)}|w_k(x) − c|. Both terms tend to 0 (steps 3–4) and the left side is ≥ 0, so ∫_{B_R(0)}|u_k − c| → 0 (squeeze_zero' / tendsto_of_tendsto_of_tendsto_of_le_of_le'). ∎
